judge: Ines — art director (typography, rhythm, hierarchy, spacing, color, iconography, dark-theme craft, density, empty/loading/error states, mobile layout)
first_five_minutes:
Cassy opens the demo on her laptop. The home page lands well: Cormorant at 56px, "Good morning, Cassandra." in italic, a warm olive-and-gold room that feels like a study rather than a SaaS console. Her eye goes to the six metric tiles — and snags. Five tiles put the label and the DEMO chip on one line; "Open opportunities" wraps its chip to a second line, so the big serif "7" sits a full line lower than "24.8k" beside it. The row is out of rhythm before she has read a word. Four tiles have a sparkline, two don't. Then the Raven briefing, which is beautiful — until she tries to read it: the summary paragraph under that 49px headline is 11px. So is every page's subtitle. So is the proposed brief she is meant to approve at her desk. She'll lean in, and she'll feel her eyes doing it.

She clicks into The Universe. This is the best screen in the product: eight placeholder covers, colour-coded by series, each honestly labelled "CATALOG PLACEHOLDER · NOT OFFICIAL COVER", every card saying "Metadata needs verification". She opens Assassin's Refusal. The metadata list is clean, then "Details to add" opens onto thirteen 11px pills wrapping across two rows, and the panel under them is a 300px-tall card holding two sentences. The "Prepare book details" button is a 1,085px-wide gold bar — it reads as a banner, not a button.

She goes to Learn & Create because the name is inviting. The first thing she sees is a broken control: "Five quick lessons, when you need them" shows the browser's default ▶ triangle and then the designed chevron drops onto its own line below. Under it, four "starting role" cards with stark white operating-system radio buttons — the only pure white in the whole app, because nothing declares `color-scheme: dark`. She clicks Marketing Plans: a 1,150px-wide card containing one heading, one sentence and one button, then a thousand pixels of nothing.

If she opens it on her phone — and she will, tomorrow, in front of Michael — the home metric tiles are three-across at 390px, labels wrapping to two lines, DEMO chips wrapping under them, numerals landing at four different heights. And if she ever reaches the Ads page, the H1 "Ads & next steps" is set in the sans while the empty-state headline right below it is in the serif: two display faces on one screen, because `--font-display` is referenced in three stylesheets and defined in none.

scores.verdict: Defaults genuinely favour her and the gates are explained as workflow rather than permission-seeking — but she cannot remove her own manuscript from her own workspace, and the UI says so twice on the same page.

top_findings.title: `--font-display` is used in three stylesheets and defined in none — the Ads H1, the Studio demo H2 and the book-knowledge workbench silently lose the serif
top_findings.problem: `var(--font-display)` appears in components/kira/ads/dashboard.css:1 (.ads-heading h1), components/kira/studio.css:3 (.studio-jobs-preview h2) and components/kira/library.css:90 (.knowledge-intro h3, .knowledge-reading > header h3). The token is never declared, so each `font-family` declaration is invalid at computed-value time and the element inherits Manrope. cdesktop-ads.png shows the result plainly: the page H1 "Ads & next steps" is sans at 58px while the empty-state headline directly beneath it is Cormorant. Two display faces on one screen.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add `--font-display: "Cormorant Garamond", Georgia, serif;` to `:root` alongside `--gold` and `--wine` (app/globals.css:29-31), and add a `@theme inline` alias if Tailwind utilities should reach it.

top_findings.title: 11px is the de-facto body size: 95 `--text-xs` uses plus 55 literal 11px and 56 literal 10px, including the brief she must read to approve
top_findings.problem: `--text-xs: 11px` is applied to the approval draft body (`.approval-draft pre`, :1686, re-asserted at :2537 for mobile), every page subtitle (`.page-heading p`, :486 and :2300), every form label (`.form-label`, :1793), every form error (`.form-error`, :1797), the creative-firewall table (`.policy-list > div`, :1851), the settings grid (:1828), the raven briefing summary (:679) and the recommendation card body — and a block commented "Legibility refinements for compact editorial surfaces" (:2630-2639) re-pins three of them at 11px. The mobile query relaxes nothing; it re-declares 11px. There is no real type scale, only 11/12/14/16.
top_findings.proposed_change: Set `--text-xs: 12px; --text-sm: 13px; --text-base: 15px; --text-lg: 17px;` and delete the literal 11px re-declarations at :486, :1665, :1686, :1793, :1797, :1851, :2300, :2352, :2537 and :2630-2639, promoting reading copy to `--text-sm`/`--text-base` and keeping 11px only for eyebrows, kbd and origin badges.

top_findings.title: No `color-scheme: dark` anywhere, so every native control renders in light mode on a near-black page
top_findings.problem: `grep -rn color-scheme app components` returns nothing; `html` carries only Tailwind's `.dark` class (app/layout.tsx:95). Chromium therefore paints all UA widgets for a light surface: the four white radios on /learn (learn-page.tsx:163), the light chevrons and popups on the `<select>`s in /plans (plans-page.tsx:77,80,86), /access (access-page.tsx:134,147) and /connections, the `mm/dd/yyyy` date field and calendar glyph on /plans (plans-page.tsx:81) whose placeholder computes to roughly 4.0:1 against #121312, the file picker on the manuscript page, and the scrollbars.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add `color-scheme: dark;` to the `:root` block at app/globals.css:9, and add a custom chevron background to the shared select rule at :3406 so the control reads as designed rather than merely dark.

top_findings.title: Metric tiles lose their baseline whenever the DEMO chip wraps — visible on desktop and in four of six tiles on mobile
top_findings.problem: `.metric-top` is `display:flex; justify-content:space-between; flex-wrap:wrap` holding the label and `<DemoBadge/>` (metric-card.tsx:15-19). When the label is long ("Open opportunities"), the chip drops to a second line and pushes the 40px serif numeral down, so the six-tile row on desktop-home.png has two different value baselines. At 390px the grid is still three-across (the two-column rule sits behind `@media (max-width: 380px)`, :2583), so labels wrap to two lines, chips wrap under them, and the tiles land at four different heights.
top_findings.proposed_change: `.metric-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; }`, `.metric-top { min-height: 2lh; align-items: flex-start; flex-wrap: nowrap; }`, `.metric-top > span:first-child { min-width: 0; }`, `.metric-value { margin-top: auto; }`; and move the two-column breakpoint from 380px to 560px (or make the base grid `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(150px, 1fr))` at :538).

top_findings.title: The manuscript page — the most intimate screen in the product — is a two-equal-column grid with ~760px of empty column
top_findings.problem: `.library-detail-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; align-items: start; }` pairs a card that usually holds two sentences ("Your book, in your words.", connected-book-detail.tsx:137) against the consent + upload card that runs to ~1,300px (line 141-149). In cdesktop-universe-assassins-refusal.png the left column stops at 540px and the rest is void. The "Prepare book details" button below it spans 1,085px as a full-bleed bar.
top_findings.proposed_change: Single-column the grid (`grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr)`) so the description card sits full width above the manuscript card, and cap the primary actions with `.book-materials-card [data-slot="button"], .library-panel > [data-slot="button"] { justify-self: start; width: auto; }`.

top_findings.title: Loading, error and empty states repeatedly drop out of the design system into bare paragraphs
top_findings.problem:
The connected Plans error is a plain wine box with no icon, no heading and no inline retry (`

`, :52), while a good failure language already exists in `.failure-state` (globals.css:3608, used by app/error.tsx:12). Loading is a naked `

` in at least five places: plans-page.tsx:53, connected-home.tsx:102, connected-library.tsx:68, studio-page.tsx:204 and 218, connected-book-detail.tsx:133 and 173. Skeleton exists and is used in exactly two files (app/loading.tsx, opportunities-page.tsx:20). The demo /plans page (plans-page.tsx:48) and the connected Studio history (studio-page.tsx:218) render as a bare card or a single sentence above hundreds of pixels of void.
top_findings.proposed_change: Standardise three shared blocks and use them everywhere: `.failure-state` for page errors (icon + eyebrow + heading + message + inline retry wired to the page's own `load()`), Skeleton grids shaped like the content for loading (book grid, plan cards, studio list), and the composed `.empty-state`/`.ads-empty` treatment for empties. Convert plans-page.tsx:52-53,60,121-124,131-132, studio-page.tsx:204,218, connected-library.tsx:68, connected-home.tsx:102 and connected-book-detail.tsx:133,173.

top_findings.title: Broken disclosure control at the top of Learn & Create: native ▶ marker plus a chevron that wraps to its own line
top_findings.problem: `.learn-lessons-panel > summary` sets only cursor, padding, min-height, colour and weight. It never removes the list marker and never becomes a flex row, so the summary at learn-page.tsx:147 — which contains a `<span>` and a `ChevronDown` — renders the browser triangle and drops the designed chevron onto a second line. The inner `.learn-lesson summary` two rules away (:3434-3437) does all of this correctly.
top_findings.proposed_change: `.learn-lessons-panel > summary { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; list-style: none; }`, `.learn-lessons-panel > summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }`, `.learn-lessons-panel[open] > summary svg { transform: rotate(180deg); }`.

top_findings.title: Owner email collides with the OWNER pill on Workspace access
top_findings.problem: `.access-owner` is a plain block with only padding and a border, while access-page.tsx:142 renders `{email}OWNER` as two inline elements with no separator. In cdesktop-access.png "cassie-fixture@example.test" butts directly against the pill with zero space; the two read as one string.
top_findings.proposed_change: `.access-owner { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 10px 12px; }` and give the trailing `.quiet-note` `flex-basis: 100%`.

top_findings.title: 7px type and 28px tap targets at the small end
top_findings.problem: `@media (max-width: 380px)` sets `.cover-placeholder { font-size: 7px; }`, so the "CATALOG PLACEHOLDER · NOT OFFICIAL COVER" provenance line — the label that keeps the decorative covers honest — is unreadable on an iPhone SE. Separately `.book-tabs-list [data-slot="tabs-trigger"]` (:1607) is 11px with 7px/11px padding, giving ~28px targets across thirteen wrapping tabs, and the mobile override at :2513 shrinks the padding further to 8px/9px.
top_findings.proposed_change: Delete the 7px override at :2601-2602 (let it inherit the ~9px rule at :2490 or hide the line below 380px), and raise the tab triggers to `min-height: 44px; padding: 10px 14px; font-size: 13px;` while removing the shrinking override at :2513.

top_findings.title: Full-bleed primary buttons flatten the hierarchy on four screens
top_findings.problem: "Prepare book details" renders as a 1,085px gold bar (book-detail.tsx:133-136 inside `.book-materials-card`), "Grant access" as a 535px bar (access-page.tsx), "Save link" as a 525px bar (connections-page.tsx), "Copy for NotebookLM" likewise. A gold rectangle that wide stops reading as a button and becomes a banner, and it leaves the card with no visual centre.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add `.book-materials-card [data-slot="button"], .access-form [data-slot="button"], .connection-form [data-slot="button"], .notebook-bridge [data-slot="button"] { justify-self: start; width: auto; }` (keeping `.learn-save-button`'s full width, which is deliberate inside a narrow column).

top_findings.title: Zero renders as the letter O in the desk's serif counter
top_findings.problem: `.memory-count strong` sets Cormorant Garamond at 46px (globals.css:1755-1759) and desk-page.tsx:147 prints `{feedback.length}` directly, so a fresh workspace shows a 46px Cormorant zero beside "lessons saved" — in desktop-desk.png it reads as "O lessons saved". The connected home already solves this properly by rendering an em-dash for zero (connected-home.tsx:171).
top_findings.proposed_change: Mirror connected-home.tsx:171: render `{feedback.length > 0 ? feedback.length : "—"}` and move the count to a caption ("No lessons saved yet"), or add `font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums;` to `.memory-count strong` and `.community-stats strong`.

top_findings.title: Half the stylesheets are hand-minified and the palette is ~200 untokenised hex values
top_findings.problem: components/kira/plans.css is a single 3,400-character line and components/kira/ads/dashboard.css is four; library.css is half formatted and half minified. Meanwhile `:root` (globals.css:9-33) defines nine colour tokens while the sheets hard-code roughly two hundred one-off hexes (#3a2227, #945c61, #394132, #4c5743, #b8cdbd, #dcc1cf…). Nothing in the system can be adjusted in one place, which is why the same component reads differently on different pages.
top_findings.proposed_change: Re-format plans.css, ads/dashboard.css and the minified half of library.css as multi-line CSS, then lift the recurring surface, hairline, panel and accent values onto `:root` as `--surface-1/2`, `--hairline`, `--accent-story/readers` and use `color-mix()` for the tints.

what_works: The type pairing is a real point of view: Cormorant Garamond for display against Manrope for interface, with italic `<em>` as the second line of nearly every headline ("The evidence is here. / *The call is yours.*"). It reads as a book designer's decision, not a template's.

The dark palette is warm and specific — olive-gold rather than the usual blue-grey — and it holds across almost every surface. `--gold #c7af83`, `--wine #753a47`, backgrounds around #121312/#191a18. Nothing about it says generic SaaS.

The raven line-art in the briefing card (components/kira/raven-art.tsx) and the huge ghosted "03" behind the telescope on the roadmap previews (app/[module]/page.tsx:127-130, globals.css:1901 `font-size: 250px`) are genuine moments of delight that cost nothing and never tip into kitsch.

The placeholder book covers are the best-executed idea in the product: series-coloured, set in the display face, and honestly captioned "CATALOG PLACEHOLDER · NOT OFFICIAL COVER" on the artwork itself (desktop-universe.png). They give an empty catalog visual presence without pretending to be real.

Provenance has a consistent visual language — the outlined DEMO / PUBLIC SOURCE / MANUAL SNAPSHOT / NEEDS VERIFICATION chips share one form and vary only by colour family (globals.css:585-609). It is disciplined enough that she will learn it in a minute.

The connected home's zero states are exactly right: an em-dash with a caption rather than a "0" (connected-home.tsx:170-175), and a completed step renders a check in place of its numeral (getting-started.tsx:148).

Card rhythm and vertical spacing on Mission Control, Briefings and the demo Universe are confident and unhurried — generous card padding (24-28px), a clear eyebrow/headline/body stack, and a footer that sets expectations quietly rather than shouting.

Focus and motion craft are carefully handled: a 2px gold focus ring with 4px offset on every link, button and summary (globals.css:98-102), a working skip link (:1929), and a blanket `prefers-reduced-motion` rule (:2620).

The custom checkbox is properly made — appearance reset, a clip-path tick, gold fill on check, its own focus ring and a disabled state — and it is shared across the library, plans and studio (globals.css:3602-3607). It shows the system can be done well when someone does it.
The Ads empty state (`.ads-empty` with its orbit glyph, radial ground and serif headline) and the 404 page are what every other empty state in the app should be modelled on.
